tools.name: search_local_workers
tools.description: Search for local workers on GigNGo by service category and location. Returns public worker profiles (name, bio, skills, rates, rating, review count, service area, profile URL) sorted by rating. Use list_service_categories first if you are unsure of the service slug. State is the full state name in l

tools.name: get_worker_profile
tools.description: Get the full public profile of a single GigNGo worker by their profile slug. Returns display name, bio, skills, per-skill rates, rating, review count, badges, service area, availability, and a shareable profile URL. Slugs come from search_local_workers results (the "slug" field) or from gigngo.org/w

tools.name: list_service_categories
tools.description: List all 30 GigNGo service categories with their slugs (e.g. "house-cleaning", "electrician", "moving-help"). Call this to discover valid values for the `service` parameter of search_local_workers and the `category` parameter of browse_open_tasks.

tools.name: check_service_availability
tools.description: Check which of the 30 service categories have active workers in a US state or city, with worker counts per service. Useful before searching, or to answer "can I get X done in Y?". State is required (full name, lowercase, hyphens: "new-jersey"); city is optional — omit it for state-level availability

tools.name: browse_open_tasks
tools.description: Browse open consumer tasks (jobs) posted on GigNGo that workers can apply to. tools.name: get_area_demand_density
tools.description: Find which US cities are actually converting: how many jobs each area posted, how many locals applied, what share of jobs got any reply at all, and the median hours to the first applicant. Ranked by a "heat" score that combines applicant density with response reliability, shrunk toward the platform

tools.name: get_platform_info
tools.description: Get an overview of the GigNGo platform: what it is, service category count, US coverage, iOS/Android app links, and API documentation URLs. Call this for general "what is GigNGo" questions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_local_workers, get_worker_profile, get_platform_info · Public sink: get_area_demand_density.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_local_workers, get_worker_profile, get_platform_info · Public sink: get_area_demand_density

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
